liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Supplication** (3 reviews): Playing in the Band into Supplication and back out again is called sweetness by the reviewer; Supplication here is loose; many versions are tighter, with better-hit notes and lyrics, though still bearable [5][10][14]
- **Slipknot!** (2 reviews): Slipknot! runs at hyper speed, its closing theme at least twice as fast as usual, yet they land cleanly in Franklin's; Band loses track of the Slipknot! ending and it collapses; Keith steps in to signal where they are [5][11]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Crowd roars as the first chords of Franklin's Tower emerge from the messy Slipknot! ending; Keith improvises in this Franklin's Tower more than in all of early 1978, especially near the end [11][12]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Stella Blue sounds like the band is rushing through it, with little feeling; Keith adds a beautiful flourish right at the close of Stella Blue [9][12]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): The transition from Playing In The Band into Supplication is interesting [10]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 other source): A 1:14 patch from the other source near the end of Samson is the only large one [2]
- **Drums** (1 review): The drumming includes some cool break-beat passages [14]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): The end of Franklin's and the opening of The Music Never Stopped are singled out as glorious [12]

## The recordings

- **gd76-09-24.aud.unknown.16901.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 4.42/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is very listenable; Sound is flat, and Phil is barely audible [8][9]
- **gd1976-09-24.147381.aud-unk.flac1644**: audience recording; 24 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Lo-fi stereo sound with tight edits; many songs are clipped at the start or end [2]

## Around the show

- William and Mary Hall holds 11,300 seats [8]
- A commenter says the Dead moved to Hampton in 1979 and never played William and Mary Hall again [13]
- This Slipknot! is less tight than some versions played the following year [5]
- Reviewer thinks the hall's acoustics seem better than those of the circular Hampton Coliseum [6]
- Reviewer finds the June and July 1976 shows better than this one [9]
- Reviewer finds the hall's acoustics better than the circular Hampton Coliseum's [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-09-24.aud.unknown.16901.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Audience reel to 48k DATs, then Midiman Delta DiO 2496, CoolEdit2000, wav, and finally shn [1]
- **gd1976-09-24.147381.aud-unk.flac1644**: taped by Unknown via Richie & Rip; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD of unknown lineage > lo-gen cassette via Richie & Rip. [2]. Also: Alternate stereo audience source to ID-16901; tape breaks during playback were patched with bits from ID-16901 [2]
- Audience reel to 48k DATs, Midiman Delta DiO 2496, CoolEdit2000, wav, then shn [19]
